title: chore(deps): upgrade CoW widget stack and drop @cowprotocol/events force-pin
description:
## What it solves

Upgrades the CoW Protocol widget stack to current versions and removes the long-standing `@cowprotocol/events` force-pin (`1.3.0`). This modernises a deprecated integration and, as a side effect, removes the last `protobufjs@6` / `ipfs-only-hash` transitive chain from the tree (they came in via `widget-react → cow-sdk@8 → sdk-app-data@4.6.x`).

## How this PR fixes it

- `@cowprotocol/widget-react` `1.3.5 → 3.2.2` (pulls `widget-lib@4.4.2`, `events@4.8.0`, `cow-sdk@9.2.2`, `sdk-app-data@5.x`).
- Removed the `@cowprotocol/events: "1.3.0"` resolution — our code now tracks the current events API.
- Migrated the events API in `SwapWidget`:
  - `CowEvents` → `CowWidgetEvents`, `CowEventListeners` → `CowWidgetEventListeners`. Imported with aliases (`as CowEvents` / `as CowEventListeners`) to keep the call sites and diff minimal.
  - `OnTradeParamsPayload.orderType` is now `@cowprotocol/types`' `UiOrderType` (adds `HOOKS`/`YIELD`), nominally distinct from our local Jest-safe `UiOrderType` duplicate. Mapped at the widget boundary by value (`UiOrderType[orderType as keyof typeof UiOrderType] ?? SWAP`) so the shared enums/helpers stay untouched. Given `enabledTradeTypes` is restricted to SWAP/LIMIT/ADVANCED, `HOOKS`/`YIELD` won't be emitted; the fallback is defensive.
  - `OnTradeParamsPayload` fields are now `Partial`, so `sell/buy.asset` fall back to `''` (the existing "no asset" convention).
- `fee.ts`: `TokenInfo` fields are optional in the new payload, so the stablecoin lookup guards `undefined` before indexing.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pinned `widget-react` to exact `3.2.2`: it and its `4.4.2`/`4.8.0` siblings are past the repo's 7-day age gate, while the newest wave (Jul 30) is quarantined. Caret ranges resolve transitive deps to the newest past-gate versions automatically.
- This branch does not dedupe the two remaining `protobufjs@7` copies (Trezor + Firebase gRPC) — that's the separate protobufjs-resolution PR. After this lands, that resolution can target 7.x cleanly with no v6 left.

## How to test it

1. `yarn install`, then open the Swap feature on web.
2. Verify the CoW widget mounts, theming (light/dark) applies, and network/token selection works.
3. Change trade params (SWAP/LIMIT/TWAP) and confirm the widget fee updates and the recipient/trade-type state syncs (the `ON_CHANGE_TRADE_PARAMS` path).
4. Create an order and confirm toast/order lifecycle events still update swap order status (`ON_TOAST_MESSAGE` path).
5. `yarn workspace @safe-global/web type-check` and swap unit tests pass (verified locally: 59/59).

## Screenshots

_Add a before/after screenshot of the swap widget rendering._

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱
- [ ] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊
- [ ] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻

---

findings.claim: The code looks up the order type by enum name (UiOrderType[params.orderType as keyof typeof UiOrderType]), but the adjacent comment says the lookup is by value; this only works because the local enum's names happen to equal its values, and an inherited property name such as 'constructor' would not be nullish and would skip the intended fallback to SWAP, though this can only be triggered by a value outside the widget's own typed payload.
widget-react@3.2.2 requires exactly react 19.1.2, while the web app uses react 19.2.0; this mismatch predates the change but could still produce install warnings worth watching for.

apps/web imports @cowprotocol/events directly in SwapWidget/index.tsx, helpers/utils.ts and helpers/fee.ts but does not declare it as a dependency, relying instead on it arriving transitively through @cowprotocol/widget-lib; with the root package.json resolution pinning it to 1.3.0 now removed, the version apps/web compiles against depends on Yarn's hoisting, so a future widget bump could silently change event names or types. Adding @cowprotocol/events as an explicit dependency, pinned to the lockfile version, would prevent this.

The package @cowprotocol/events is imported (including in this diff's new import) but is not declared as a dependency in apps/web/package.json; the diff also removes the root version pin, so the version apps/web compiles against now depends on whatever range widget-react requires, and the import only resolves because the node-modules linker hoists it.
The test 'does not silently reset LIMIT/TWAP to SWAP' duplicates the assertions already made by the preceding test, which shows LIMIT maps to LIMIT and TWAP maps to TWAP.

isStableCoin now guards against a missing token address, changing prior behavior where buyToken?.address.toLowerCase() would throw if buyToken existed but lacked an address; since the CoW v4 payload makes that field optional, this change is needed to avoid crashing the ON_CHANGE_TRADE_PARAMS handler, but it is not covered by any test.

fee.test.ts was not updated as part of this PR and none of its existing cases pass a token without an address, so a case (e.g. calculateFeePercentageInBps with buyToken: {} or sellToken: undefined) should be added asserting the call does not throw and returns the non-stablecoin fee tier.

The enum lookup `UiOrderType[params.orderType as keyof typeof UiOrderType] ?? UiOrderType.SWAP` reads a string taken from a cross-origin widget payload directly off the enum object, so a value like 'constructor', 'toString' or '__proto__' resolves to an inherited Object.prototype member instead of undefined, bypassing the SWAP fallback and letting a function value flow into UiOrderTypeToOrderType and setSwapParams. Using Object.values().includes(), Object.hasOwn(), or a Map instead would avoid this and remove the need for the 'as keyof' cast.

The test 'does not silently reset LIMIT/TWAP to SWAP' can only fail if the mapping test above it (lines 433-437) also fails, so it adds no additional coverage and should be dropped or merged into that test.

The makePayload test helper casts its fixture with 'as unknown as OnTradeParamsPayload' rather than using a properly typed helper (e.g. based on Partial<OnTradeParamsPayload>), which loses type checking of the fixture against the v4 payload type.

The fix for the crash where buyToken?.address.toLowerCase() threw when buyToken had no address is not covered by any test, since every case in fee.test.ts passes a string address for both tokens, so reverting the fix would not cause any test to fail.

The new test covering the SWAP fallback for an unknown orderType only exercises the value 'SOMETHING_NEW', so it does not exercise inherited-property keys such as 'constructor' and would not catch the enum lookup issue; a test case using such a key should be added.
